sourceEvidence.label: A90 current contracts, selected SD-free design, H24 SD consumers, Wi-Fi profile producer, property consumer, and evidence path
sourceEvidence.sourceRefreeze: Rebound after WP-H0-1 and the GOAL_A90 WP-H0-2 H0-only status update

assessment.summary: A90 should replace the remaining SD evidence and compatibility inputs with four typed channels. The selected design reuses the public-key validation pattern, requires a new separately authorized immutable-generation Wi-Fi provisioner, eliminates or minimizes the Android property seed, and makes native the sole device-side evidence writer.

nonNegotiables: H24 remains installed and healthy; its consumed D1 is never replayed.
Only boot may be a partition payload; UFS root content remains read-only and this analysis grants no UFS mutation.
Wi-Fi secrets, public client keys, server private keys, compatibility state, and evidence do not share a generic mutable namespace.
No successor identity is allocated until SD evidence and property dependencies plus the producer boundary are closed.
No private input, raw credential, device identifier, or raw run evidence enters public Git.
Rollback, physical recovery, durable no-replay, attendance, and target isolation remain exact.

opportunities.title: Separate A90 SD-free inputs from evidence and minimize compatibility state
opportunities.summary: Remove the hard SD evidence bind and property snapshot without embedding long-lived secrets into boot or recreating one broad mutable cache bundle.

sourceEvidence.claim: H24 publishes the run identity and reads Debian evidence under /mnt/sdext.
The handoff path hard-gates a bind of the SD evidence directory into Debian before Wi-Fi handoff and root transition.
H24 compiles a property root under /mnt/sdext.
Native Wi-Fi configuration has SD-primary and cache-fallback readers and keeps inline secrets out of the profile grammar.
A public legacy host tool can stage cache profiles and secrets, but performs live NCM/tcpctl device mutation.
Current A90 D1 rules do not grant generic persistent credential/configuration mutation and H24 commands need separately reviewed authority.
The builder already validates and embeds one canonical public Ed25519 authorization key without treating private bytes as an artifact input.
The selected design calls for native-only cache receipts, strict host observation, and a per-boot child-private server host key.
Property/service minimization and typed inputs are shared prerequisites for both the current native-supervisor baseline and clean Debian relaunch research.

desiredInvariants: Every input has one exact typed root, schema, writer, reader, lifetime, and authority.
The boot artifact contains only public client authorization and no Wi-Fi or SSH private key.
Wi-Fi profiles are immutable selected generations; active files are never edited in place.
Credential provisioning is a separate attended one-use capability with no arbitrary path, shell, or command authority.
The Android property channel is absent or an exact minimal deterministic seed; a full private snapshot is rejected.
The server private key is generated once per boot inside child-private tmpfs and only public fingerprint data leaves it.
Native PID 1 is the sole device-side receipt writer and Debian has no write path to the receipt root.
Native and host observations are joined only by exact target, resident, boot, run, pidfd, input-generation, and receipt digests.
All records and generation publications are durable, bounded, no-clobber, crash-reconcilable, and never replay uncertain effects.
No reachable successor artifact, runtime path, or health predicate requires /mnt/sdext.

options.title: Private boot bundle
options.summary: Embed the Wi-Fi credential and full compatibility input in a private candidate boot artifact alongside the public client key.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It can remove SD runtime reads, but only by moving private state into the candidate.
The existing builder pattern is safe for a public key; extending it to persistent secrets changes the trust boundary.
The full property snapshot remains unproved even if embedded.

tradeoffs.assessment: Persistent Wi-Fi secrets enter candidate, rollback, build, and archival custody.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove zero public/log leakage and complete private artifact custody; rejection remains preferred.

tradeoffs.assessment: Inputs may be locally available during boot, but ramdisk decompression and copy costs are unmeasured.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure artifact bytes, decompression time, boot reads, and input-copy latency.

tradeoffs.assessment: The boot bundle and runtime copies may coexist at peak.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak bootstrap RSS/PSS and tmpfs bytes.

tradeoffs.assessment: A separate provisioner disappears, but credential rotation becomes a new F1 and rollback-artifact problem.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise rotation, failed boot, rollback, and stale artifact rejection.

tradeoffs.assessment: Routine credential rotation requires building, qualifying, approving, and installing a boot artifact.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure complete attended rotation and recovery workload.

tradeoffs.assessment: It reuses the builder input mechanism but expands it beyond its public-key safety purpose.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run a private-artifact threat review before considering implementation.

residualRisks: Credential rotation is coupled to F1.
Private bytes multiply across candidate and rollback custody.
The full property snapshot remains unbounded.

acceptanceCriteria: No private byte enters public Git or logs.
migrationNotes: This option is rejected and is included to make the shortcut explicit.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Use only the exact reviewed boot rollback; credential rollback remains coupled to it.

options.title: Wholesale cache transplant
options.summary: Move the current SD profile, secret, property, and evidence trees to cache and adapt the legacy staging path.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A cache Wi-Fi consumer path already exists.
A prototype producer exists, but lacks production authority, generations, and no-replay semantics.
Moving the full property snapshot does not establish its minimum or safety.
The legacy live staging surface has no current credential-mutation authority.

tradeoffs.assessment: It removes removable-media dependence but preserves a broad mutable trust plane and generic command surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Split roots and writers, replace active overwrite semantics, and independently review the live provision boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cache may be faster than SD, but exact bytes and fsync latency are unknown.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure provisioning, boot reads, property materialization, and write amplification.

tradeoffs.assessment: The same full property tree and runtime consumers remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure property-tree resident pages and setup peak.

tradeoffs.assessment: SD absence stops being a failure, but replace-in-place and partial transfer states remain ambiguous.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Power-cut every transfer and publication prefix and prove no replay.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing operator tooling is familiar, but it lacks a current production authority model.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Demonstrate exact generation rollback without arbitrary shell/path access.

tradeoffs.assessment: It has the smallest code delta and the largest inherited security debt.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Bind and review every retained legacy command and dependency.

residualRisks: One mutable cache domain can influence credentials, privileged compatibility, and grading.
The full property snapshot remains unproved.
The current stager has no activated A90 authority and no immutable generation rollback.

migrationNotes: Rejected for production; parser and format evidence may be reused host-only.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Unspecified in the legacy path; this is a blocking deficiency.

options.title: Typed minimal channels
options.summary: Separate public auth, persistent Wi-Fi secrets, minimal compatibility state, native receipts, and per-boot server-key lifetime into independently bound channels.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Native-only cache receipts remove the SD bind and Debian evidence writer.
Property state becomes absent or a minimal deterministic seed rather than a full snapshot.
The parser concepts are reusable, but successor precedence and immutable generation semantics change.
Secret grammar and redaction lessons are reusable; live transport and replace semantics are not.
Provisioning is explicitly separated into a future independently reviewed capability.
The canonical public-key validation pattern is retained for public input only.
It implements the selected native receipt, host observation, and per-boot key lifetime split.
The schemas can be shared by either WLAN ownership architecture after property/service ablation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Secrets, public auth, compatibility state, and evidence have distinct writers/readers and cannot silently authorize one another.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model every channel and prove cross-channel read/write/rename/FD/IPC denial.

tradeoffs.assessment: Generation and receipt fsyncs add bounded cost while SD and possibly a full property snapshot disappear.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure bytes, fsync latency, write amplification, WLAN readiness, and authenticated SSH readiness.

tradeoffs.assessment: A minimal or absent property seed can reduce mappings; runtime secret and receipt buffers add small bounded state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure property pages, runtime input tmpfs, receipt buffers, and peak/steady RSS/PSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Immutable generations and native-only records remove in-place credential and shared-evidence ambiguity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Power-cut every prepare/select/record prefix and reconcile without resend or broad cleanup.

tradeoffs.assessment: The initial workflow is more explicit, but rotation, diagnosis, and rollback have attributable generations and records.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Time provision, rotation, rollback, no-SD D0, failed handoff, and attended recovery drills.

tradeoffs.assessment: It requires new schemas, validators, provision authority, readers, property ablation, receipt writer, and retrieval.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Deliver host-only schemas and simulators first, then independent closure review before identity allocation.

residualRisks: The exact property minimum is unproved.
The exact safe live credential provision transport is unselected.
At-rest PSK confidentiality has no hardware-backed proof.
Cache wear, corruption, free-space reserve, and performance are unmeasured.
The native receipt codec and read-only retrieval are unimplemented.

affectedComponents: Wi-Fi input schema and native reader
vendor property dependency and seed producer
native evidence writer and read-only retrieval
host SSH observer and evidence join
workPackages: Freeze typed schemas and threat model.
Build host-only generation transaction and receipt simulators.
Implement typed readers and native-only receipt without a candidate identity.
Design and independently review a separate credential provision authority.
Review the full execution-critical closure before allocating a successor.
acceptanceCriteria: No reachable successor path or predicate references /mnt/sdext.
No boot artifact, log, receipt, or public file contains private credentials.
The property input is absent or an exact minimal deterministic seed.
Provision and receipt crash-prefix tests never replay or overwrite uncertain effects.
Debian cannot write or name the native receipt root.
A healthy SD-free resident and attended no-SD D0 precede any handoff approval.
migrationNotes: The existing cache profile parser and public-key validator are evidence, not live authority.
The legacy tcpctl profile stager is not reused as the production provisioner.
The same typed inputs support either native-supervisor or clean Debian-supervisor WLAN ownership after separate H0 selection.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain the prior immutable Wi-Fi generation until successor resident health and no-SD D0 close; use only the exact reviewed boot rollback for candidate failure.

opportunities.recommendation: Select typed minimal channels for H0 schema, property-ablation, and simulator work. Do not activate a credential provisioner or allocate a successor until the new higher-precedence and A90 target-contract boundary is independently reviewed.
validationPlan: Reject every reachable /mnt/sdext path in the successor closure and artifacts.
Prove boot artifacts contain public authorization only and no private credentials or full property snapshot.
Exercise immutable Wi-Fi generation publication, selector, rollback, and every crash prefix without replay.
Prove property input absent or exactly minimal and deterministic.
Prove Debian has zero path, mount, FD, IPC, or rename capability to native receipts.
Join native and host evidence only on exact target, resident, boot, run, pidfd, generation, receipt, and host-key bindings.
Measure storage bytes, fsync latency, write amplification, boot/WLAN/SSH latency, memory, CPU, wakeups, power, and recovery time.
After a future healthy resident install, require attended physical SD removal and exact no-SD D0 before D1.
